consensus_summary: All ten stakeholders — spanning Clinical Affairs, Compliance, Utilization Management, Finance, Pharmacy, Behavioral Health, and Patient/Family representation — agree that the underlying clinical case is compelling and that outright denial is not warranted given the documented end-organ progression, exhausted pharmacologic ladder, and credible cost-offset trajectory. However, no stakeholder supports approval as submitted. The dominant convergence point is the step-therapy gap: the six-month supervised weight management requirement is unmet by one documented session, and every reviewer without exception insists this be resolved through a formal, policy-anchored exception process with documented medical director sign-off — not a discretionary waiver or quiet approval. The Nephrology Clinical Advisor introduced a second high-consensus concern in the reassessment round: the complete absence of a nephrology consult in a request whose primary organ-protection rationale is renal, and whose eGFR of 54 creates material perioperative renal risk; every stakeholder who reassessed explicitly adopted or elevated this gap as a co-equal precondition. Three additional open items were raised by subsets of reviewers but not universally resolved: the pharmacological inaccuracy in the Tirzepatide rejection rationale (flagged by the Endocrinology Clinical Consultant, Nephrology Clinical Advisor, Medical Director of Surgical & Specialty Care, and Pharmacy Benefit and Drug Policy Manager); the unverified 70–80% insulin discontinuation probability (flagged by the Finance Director, Pharmacy Benefit and Drug Policy Manager, and Client Success Director); and the absence of a post-operative hypoglycemia management protocol (flagged by the Behavioral Health and Surgical Readiness Reviewer and Raymond, the patient's caregiver advocate). No stakeholder changed their position between rounds.
key_tensions: The Finance Director's actuarial concern about Medicare transition risk and NPV transfer to CMS — framing the cost-offset case as potentially accruing to the federal program rather than the plan — was explicitly rejected as irrelevant to coverage determination by the Compliance Officer, Endocrinology Clinical Consultant, Nephrology Clinical Advisor, Medical Director of Surgical & Specialty Care, and Raymond; while acknowledged as analytically legitimate in its own lane, the majority view is that actuarial tenure probability must not influence a medical necessity determination, and several reviewers warned it could constitute pretextual denial reasoning under ACA non-discrimination provisions and state PA reform statutes.

The Pharmacy Benefit and Drug Policy Manager and Endocrinology Clinical Consultant hold that the Tirzepatide rejection rationale — which conflates SGLT2 inhibitor mechanism with GLP-1 pathway failure — constitutes an inadequately documented step-therapy exhaustion and creates denial-defense exposure; the Medical Director of Surgical & Specialty Care accepted a one-paragraph clarification from Dr. Nair as sufficient, and the Client Success Director cautioned that formally challenging the rationale in documentation would require a contradicting clinical opinion rather than mere skepticism, creating an unresolved internal disagreement about how strictly this pharmacological inaccuracy must be remedied before authorization.

The Nephrology Clinical Advisor treated the absent nephrology consult as the single most critical unresolved gap — arguing it is a clinical harm-prevention issue that cannot be remedied after the fact — while the Compliance Officer and Director of Utilization Management treated the step-therapy exception documentation as the primary blocker; the Nephrology Clinical Advisor explicitly noted that the procedural criterion can be resolved with a waiver memo whereas an acute perioperative renal insult cannot be undone, signaling a prioritization disagreement that the committee should address directly.
recommendation_rationale: The weight of stakeholder input — unanimous in round one and reinforced without exception in round two — is that the clinical case is meritorious and denial is not appropriate, but that authorization cannot proceed until four specific documentation gaps are formally closed: (1) a formal step-therapy exception determination, grounded in written plan policy or medical necessity override language and signed at the medical director level, addressing the missed June supervised weight management session due to ED hospitalization; (2) a nephrology consultation note with explicit pre-operative renal risk stratification and a post-operative renal monitoring protocol, given that the eGFR of 54 creates material perioperative risk and the organ-protection rationale centers entirely on renal outcomes; (3) a sourced, stratified evidentiary basis for the 70–80% insulin discontinuation probability claim, or revision of the cost-offset model to figures consistent with published STAMPEDE outcomes; and (4) either a clarified clinical contraindication to Tirzepatide documented by Dr. Nair with pharmacologically accurate reasoning, or a formal formulary exception determination confirming that a GLP-1/GIP trial is not required as a prior step. Given the member's documented clinical urgency — active end-organ damage, recurrent severe hypoglycemia, and declining renal function — the Director of Utilization Management's recommendation that this deferral be processed on an expedited review timeline rather than the standard 14-day window should be adopted by the committee.
